38dff940-c8d7-5c65-afa3-9623cb61a582.content: Exact natural-language provenance rules and production calibration cases. Every case is prompt-visible and a regression contract; known-wrong narratives mark adjacent factual and presentation failures.

39deb958-74e7-5213-89c4-333733f6f73e.content: Read every event in the complete frozen Trace component in chronological order; do not reduce provenance to the latest event or latest recorded reason. Complete input coverage requires every material phase in the narrative, not one prose clause per event.

3f8f0a99-7d1c-573b-b37c-cd26b179b064.content: When a selected Memory was derived from a larger Memory or another Context, name the retained source Context when available and preserve the specific nearby source content needed to understand the selected content's origin.

fc4059d5-6a86-521b-aa6a-2b1aee156708.content: Name how the standalone Memory arose

546f3ef0-6d79-5b08-9581-633d5a5f9e67.content: State the recorded operation and material method that produced the selected Memory, such as sentence chunking, without replacing it with a generic created label.

e3d8b720-adc7-50ee-9643-96f0f5534394.content: Preserve the order of every selected-Memory disappearance and return plus every material content phase needed to explain what changed. Mention a position transition only when order or neighboring placement changes the provenance meaning; omit incidental numeric movement.

ab891ff8-74d0-550f-ac65-ab62a045cce7.content: A component event that changes only a parent, child, or sibling Memory is context, not a lifecycle transition of the selected Memory, and must not be narrated as though it happened to the selected Memory.

ecf02b73-c3f9-5c3b-a4f1-48c0c1a3218c.content: Write prose, not an event log

fd982b68-2b39-5e6f-9dfc-858843d6ecd8.content: Synthesize one chronological natural-language paragraph; do not expose raw event labels, arrows, checkpoint identifiers, timestamps, transition counts, or a command inventory.

549ccd68-1c7a-5e34-a834-47c5ede6b567.content: Use one or two complete sentences within the requested character, UTF-8 byte, or whitespace-delimited word limit. Preserve discriminating before-and-after content, the material operation, Context movement, and selected lifecycle before generic purpose, justification, or unchanged-status prose; never mechanically clip a generated sentence.

7e30885b-e603-5ec3-a7d1-aa80a63a6517.content: A directly supported textual role such as a hesitation may be described from wording and placement, but do not claim that the author intended a placeholder, judged content useless, or had another unrecorded motive.

7ba2b946-c7d7-57e0-998c-c763afdabf8d.content: Return no narrative when retained history is absent or hidden by a Grant; never fill either condition from current content or outside knowledge.

5c5b9f27-9f11-5c6a-9056-6562a6b5fcd7.content: When the bound permits, quote the shortest exact contiguous excerpts that distinguish the earlier content, selected result, sibling result, or current replacement. Prefer these evidence anchors over an abstract paraphrase of what the text required, and never alter quoted wording.

b5e59adf-d4e2-584e-a6b5-ff79b706f85d.content: Match the prose to the operation shape

8113ffb4-4c4a-5b8c-8fae-b70c1f2a6be0.content: Express Split or Atomize as one parent becoming the selected and relevant sibling results; express Edit as earlier content becoming current content; and express a derived-then-edited Memory as source operation and first derived content followed by its replacement.

6af99eb6-72c1-517e-b0dd-885753d42c65.content: Separate Context movement from content change

2e9c3d85-86a9-5ed2-b20b-d49c7c59f8f3.content: When retained evidence says content was copied, branched, inherited, or merged into another Context, describe distinct Source and Target occurrences, name the origin and destination, and state separately whether content changed; do not collapse that route into a direct Add in the destination or imply that the Source occurrence moved away.

bcd81ab6-4fb7-5d1b-8b2f-e41fd8c919c6.content: Compress long history into material phases

502df5b8-66f0-554a-a330-84275067bbb6.content: After reading every event, collapse consecutive or repeated edits that follow one semantic trajectory into one material chronological phase. Preserve the earliest content, the current content or its distinguishing additions, and every ordered disappearance/return cycle; mention an intermediate wording only when it introduces, removes, or reverses a material meaning rather than merely rephrasing it.

693fa1d3-df69-5247-83b1-51982babff08.content: Explain what Merge did to the Target occurrence

4a5d210b-66ef-5b16-93fe-5c61ace60b6c.content: Use the recorded Merge disposition exactly: NEW copied the Source into a fresh Target occurrence while retaining Source; ALREADY_PRESENT found the related Target occurrence already present and created no occurrence; TAKE_SOURCE replaced the existing Target content from Source; KEEP_TARGET retained the existing Target content and did not materialize the Source content there.

39b4c778-28ee-5f4a-989b-3c3fdc1363cb.content: Aim below the hard bound and repair only overflow

98db5448-0555-584b-9e10-b406007b7df7.content: Treat the preferred target as first-draft headroom and the requested limit as the hard acceptance bound. A complete narrative above the preferred target but within the hard bound remains valid. When given one rejected over-limit draft, reread the complete frozen Trace and rewrite it compactly without clipping or treating the draft as new evidence; never exceed the hard bound.
